message.content: {"name": "build_houses_or_hotel", "parameters": {"build_plan": [{"space_key": "MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE", "kind": "HOTEL", "count": 1}, {"space_key": "BALTIC_AVENUE", "kind": "HOTEL", "count": 1}, {"space_key": "ST_CHARLES_PLACE", "kind": "HOTEL", "count": 1}], "public_message": "Upgrading. Reading won't stay comfortable.", "private_thought": "Free 12 houses (cost $200) so I can arm light blues before p2 rolls off Reading. p2 has $210 and cannot unmortgage any monopoly, so returned houses are safe. Next: unmortgage Oriental $55, Vermont $55, Connecticut $66, then build 4 houses on each ($600). Rolls 2/4/5 then kill even if a Chance card gives them $150. Med hotel ($250) also now kills. Do not trade, give cash, or end turn until light blues are built. Existing 4-house pinks/oranges and Baltic already kill $210."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for Monopoly.

I have $2314 cash and am on INDIANA_AVENUE. I own four houses on the Browns, Pinks, and Oranges. Most other properties are mortgaged.

I have two get-out-of-jail cards. Player 2 has only $210 and all properties mortgaged, so they cannot build or unmortgage anything. Players 3 and 4 are bankrupt. The bank has no houses left but still holds twelve hotels.

I am calculating rent values for the four-house properties to determine how quickly I can bankrupt player 2.

Baltic Avenue with four houses costs $320. That exceeds player 2's $210 and bankrupts them immediately. Mediterranean Avenue with four houses costs $160, so player 2 survives there. All other properties with four houses also bankrupt player 2. I just need to land on the right spaces.

I am checking the board order after Reading Railroad to plan my next move. I want to unmortgage the light blue properties and build three houses each so that player 2 lands on them with a roll of two, four, or five.

Player 2's next roll from Reading Railroad lands on St. Charles Place and States Avenue with four houses, costing $625 and $750 respectively. Those two spaces alone bankrupt them immediately.

Rolls of 7, 9, 10, and 12 from Reading Railroad also bankrupt player 2 immediately. Rolls of 2, 4, and 5 land on mortgaged light blues with no rent. Unmortgaging Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut costs $176 total. The bank has no houses left.

I realized I can build houses only by hoteling a property first, since that returns four houses to the bank. Hoteling Mediterranean and Baltic would cost $100 total. A Mediterranean hotel costs $250, which exceeds player 2's $210 and would bankrupt them immediately.

I am reconsidering the earlier strategy note against hoteling. Player 2 cannot unmortgage the red properties because they lack the cash, and they do not own the dark blue set. Hoteling Mediterranean would bankrupt them immediately, so returning houses to the bank is not a concern.

The green properties are not a concern because player 2 does not own North Carolina. Hoteling Mediterranean is therefore safe; player 2 cannot form an unmortgaged monopoly even if houses return to the bank.

I must act now before ending my turn. Player 2 is on Reading Railroad and will roll next. I will hotel a property to free houses, then unmortgage the light blues and build three houses each. I am checking whether those three houses will bankrupt player 2.

Three houses on each light blue property will bankrupt player 2. Oriental and Vermont cost $270 with three houses, while Connecticut costs $300. Two houses are too low. Building nine houses costs $450. Hoteling two properties returns eight houses, so I need to hotel three.

Hoteling two brown properties and one pink or orange property returns twelve houses. That covers the nine needed for the light blues. The total cost is $826, which I can afford.

I cannot execute all four steps in one action. I must proceed sequentially: hotel a property to free houses, then unmortgage the light blues, then build evenly across the set. The even-building rule requires equal distribution of houses within each monopoly.

I can hotel multiple properties in a single build action because the plan accepts an array. I am weighing whether arming the light blues is worth the cost, since rolls of two, four, and five from Reading Railroad only occur about twenty-two percent of the time.

The kill probability from Reading Railroad rises from fourteen in thirty-six to twenty-two in thirty-six once the light blues are armed. The downside of hoteling is minor: player two cannot use the returned houses, and the cash outlay is manageable.

I am checking the even-building rules for the brown set. Both properties currently have four houses, so hoteling one would create a two-house gap. Hotels count as five houses under standard rules. I am deciding whether to hotel both browns or just one.

A one-house gap is allowed under even-building rules, so hoteling one property in a set is valid. Hoteling Mediterranean would raise its rent to $250 and kill player 2 immediately, but that space is too far from Reading Railroad to matter. The priority remains arming the light blues before player 2 rolls.

I am weighing whether to hotel every four-house property at once. That would free twelve houses and maximize rent, though it costs $700 total.

Hoteling the other four-house properties would not change the outcome against player 2, since every one of them already kills. Only Mediterranean Avenue needs a hotel to become a guaranteed kill at $250. Hoteling Baltic would also kill, but it costs $450 instead of $50. The minimum is three hotels to free nine houses, and I should include Mediterranean so it becomes a kill square.

Hoteling two brown properties returns only eight houses. That is one short of the nine needed for three houses on each light blue. I could instead build three houses on two properties and two on the third, but that would leave Connecticut at two houses and player 2 would survive there. The probabilities of rolling two, four, or five from Reading Railroad are low enough that this uneven distribution is too risky.

I will fully arm all three light blue properties. Connecticut and Vermont each have a high probability of being landed on, while Oriental is too unlikely to warrant the extra cost. Building four houses instead of three would not improve the kill outcome.

I am weighing whether three houses are enough. A $100 windfall from a chance card would raise player 2's cash to $310, which would not be enough to survive three houses on the light blues. I will skip the extra hotel and keep three houses.

I will build four houses on each light blue property. A $100 windfall from a chance card would raise player 2's cash to $310, which three houses cannot cover. Four houses on Oriental and Vermont cost $400, and four on Connecticut cost $450. The extra cost is only $150, and I have the cash. This provides insurance against an unlikely but possible chance event.

I will hotel Mediterranean, Baltic, and one pink or orange property to free twelve houses. This costs $200 total. The third property is a pink or orange at $100, while Baltic costs only $50. Both browns are cheaper than the pinks and oranges.

Hoteling is actually cheaper than four houses for street repairs. I will proceed with the build plan now.

I will pick New York Avenue as the third property to hotel. I am also considering whether to unmortgage the Reading Railroad, since player 2 is currently on it.

Railroads and utilities are not immediate threats. Player 2 cannot form a full railroad set, and utilities do not kill. I am now considering the yellow properties, but Atlantic Avenue is mortgaged and would cost $143 to unmortgage.

Unmortgaging the yellows would cost too much and is unnecessary because player 2 would need to travel most of the board to land there. Park Place should stay mortgaged since it cannot form a monopoly without Boardwalk. I will not trade with player 2 or give them cash, and I will keep my public message brief.

I will hotel three properties and skip a fourth to keep the plan simple. I am choosing St. Charles Place as the third property. Hotels are preferable to houses on the browns, so I will not need to retrieve them later. I will send a short, non-telegraphing public message such as "Enjoy Reading while it lasts."

The engine will keep asking for actions after the hotel build, so I have time to unmortgage the light blues and then build evenly across the set. Each unmortgage requires a separate action because the schema accepts only a single space key.

Unmortgaging requires no prior monopoly. The cash flow is verified: $2,114 after hotels, $1,938 after unmortgage, and $1,338 after building twelve houses. The build plan accepts multiple items, so all four light blue properties can be upgraded in one action.

I will build all three light blue properties to four houses in a single action to satisfy the even-building rule. Selling houses is too weak, and I have no need to mortgage Marvin or North Carolina. Hoteling first is correct because it frees the required houses before building. I will send a short public message: "Hotels going up."

I will keep my public message brief and avoid sounding desperate. Deception is unnecessary because the action is visible. I am reconsidering whether hoteling Mediterranean Avenue is risky, since returning houses could let player two rebuild later. However, player two cannot unmortgage a full color group, so this concern is unfounded.

Player two cannot unmortgage any color group. The reds need $385, the greens $341, and they lack a second dark blue. They have no cash to build. The housing lock is obsolete.

I will hotel only three properties in this action because the engine likely checks bank house availability before applying the plan. The remaining five hotels cost $500 and are affordable, but I am weighing whether to upgrade all of them now or save money.

Hoteling all five remaining properties would cost an extra $500, but it would make Mediterranean Avenue lethal and raise every rent. Four houses already kill player two on the other light blues, so upgrading everything is unnecessary.
